la:other:Europa.html:
Eurōpa, ae, and Eurōpe, ēs, f., = Εὐρώπη.
Daughter of the Phoenician king Agenor, sister of Cadmus, and mother of Sarpedon and Minos by Jupiter, who, under the form of a bull, carried her off to Crete, ; ; ; nom. Europe, ; ; ; gen. Europae, ; acc. Europen, ; : Europam,; .—
Poet. transf., the portico in the Field of Mars, which was adorned with a painting representing the rape of Europa, ; ; cf. .—
Hence, Eurō-paeus, a, um, adj., of or belonging to Europa: dux,i. e. Minos,.—
The continent of Europe, named after her; usual form Europa, et saep.; ; prooem. § 3; 3, 1, 1, § 5; 4, 23, 37, § 121 et saepiss.: Europe,; ; acc. Europen, ; ; .—
Derivv.
Eurōpaeus, a, um, adj., of or belonging to Europe, European: adversarii,: Scythi,.—
Eurōpensis, e, adj., the same: exercitus,: res,.

la:noun:Eurystheus.html:
Eurystheus (trisyl.), ei, m., = Εὐρυσθεύς,
son of Sthenelus and grandson of Perseus, a king of Mycenae, who, at the command of Juno, imposed upon Hercules his famous twelve labors, ; ; ; ; ; ; acc. Eurysthea, .— Hence, Eurysthēus, a, um, adj., Eurysthean, .

la:noun:Euphrates.gloss: Those who dwell on the banks of the Euphrates river.
senses: Those who dwell on the banks of the Euphrates river.
la:noun:Euphrates.html:
Euphrātes (in Inscr. also EVFRATES), is, m., = Εὐφράτης,
A wellknown river in Syria, which rises in Armenia, and, after its junction with the Tigris, empties into the Persian Gulf, now Frat, ; ; sqq.; ; ; ; abl. Euphratē, .—
Meton., the dwellers on its banks, .—Hence,
Euphrā-taeus, a, um, = Εὐφραταῖος, of the Euphrates, i. e. Armenian: diademata,.—
Euphrātis, ĭdis, f., adj., of the Euphrates: ripa,. —
A philosopher in the time of the younger Pliny, .—†
A rare Roman surname: M. IVNIVS EVFRATES, Inscr. in Bull. dell. .

senses: A philosopher in the time of Pliny the Younger.

la:other:Euander.html:
Euander (Gr. nom.-drus, ; voc. -dre, . Less correctly, Evander), dri, m., = Εὔανδρος.
Son of Carmenta (v. Carmentis), born at Pallantium, in Arcadia; he emigrated to Italy sixty years before the Trojan war, and there founded the city Pallanteum, ; ; ; ; 4, 65; 5, 91; ; ; ; 10, 515; .—Hence, Euandrĭ-us, a, um, adj., Evandrian: ensis,i. e. of Pallas, the son of Evander,: regna,i. e. Roman,: collis,i. e. the Palatine,; also, mons,.—
A Greek artist in metals, brought from Alexandria to Rome by M. Antony, Schol.; .—
An Academic philosopher, .

la:other:euge.html:
eugĕ (eugē or eugae, ), interj., = εὖγε, an exclamation of joy, applause, admiration, etc.,
well done! good! bravo! (cf. eu; freq. in Plaut. and Ter., and

in the Vulg.).

In gen.: euge, euge, perbene, Ab saxo avortit fluctus ad litus scapham,; ; ; ; et saep.; ; ; ; ; as an indecl. subst., n.: euge tuum,; : euge,well done,; .—So, eugepae (contracted from euge papae), ; ; ; ; ; .—
Esp., with an ironical signif. superadded, excellent! admirable! euge, optime, ; ; . V. Hand, Turs. II. p. 610 sq.

senses: the water-filled trench that ran around the track of the Roman circus or ran down along the centre of the racing track
la:noun:euripus.html:
eurīpus (-os), i, m., = εὔριπος,
a narrow channel, strait.
Prop.
In gen., ; ; .—
In partic.: Eurīpus, i, m., = Εὔριπος, the channel between Boeotia and Euboea, now Egripo, ; ; ; ; ; —
Transf., a canal, conduit, aqueduct.
In gen.: ductus aquarum, quos isti nilos et euripos vocant,; ; ; ; ; ; —
In partic., the trench that ran round the Roman circus, ; ; ; cf. Smith's Antiq. p. 53 a.

la:noun:Eurydice.html:
Eurўdĭce, ēs, f., = Εὐρυδίκη.
The wife of Orpheus, who died of the bite of a serpent. Orpheus obtained from Pluto permission to bring her back from the Lower World, under promise that he would not look back at her on the way. But, as he did not keep this promise, she returned to the Lower World, ; sqq.; .—
Daughter of Danaüs, .

la:other:Euclides.html:

A philosopher of Megara, a disciple of Socrates and founder of the Megaric sect, ; ; .—
A mathematician in Alexandria under Ptolemy Philadelphus, .
